sections.title: 2. Who the exam is for
sections.html:
You design, develop, test and troubleshoot solution components by using Power Platform's extension points and generative AI: custom user experiences and business logic, system integrations, data conversions, custom process automation, Power Automate workflow expressions, and agentic AI as part of solution logic.

You need applied knowledge of

  • Power Platform services, including capabilities, boundaries and constraints
  • Authentication, security and ALM
  • Developer tools, including Power Platform CLI
  • AI-assisted tools and agents for development and troubleshooting
  • Modern IDEs: Visual Studio and VS Code

You need development experience with

  • Power Platform services; JavaScript, JSON, TypeScript, Power Fx
  • C#, Python, HTML, YAML
  • RESTful web APIs; Microsoft Azure
  • Microsoft Foundry and Microsoft Copilot Studio

Python, YAML, Foundry and Copilot Studio were added to the candidate profile for AB-400.

sections.title: 4. How to read the skills measured
sections.html:
• The bullets illustrate how a skill is assessed; related topics may appear (Microsoft's own note). Treat each bullet as a heading for everything around it.
  • Most questions cover generally available (GA) features, but Preview features can appear when they're commonly used. In this guide, Preview marks anything the current documentation labels preview, so you can weigh it.
  • Expect scenario questions (choose the best component, identity, pattern or fix), code/CLI reading questions (spot the bug, pick the missing call or command), and decision-table questions (X vs Y). Exact names matter: stage numbers, message names, headers, CLI verbs, package names, limits.
  • Case studies present a business scenario followed by several questions; Microsoft's break rules differ inside case-study and problem/solution sets. Read the requirements and constraints once, then answer each question against them.

sections.title: 4. What this means for your preparation
sections.html:
If you already studied for PL-400

  • Keep ~60% of your plan for refresh: plug-ins, platform APIs, integrations, PCF, client scripting.
  • Add focused blocks for the new areas: code apps, Foundry/MCP/Work IQ, managed identity, background operations, Python SDK, generative pages and MCP app widgets.
  • Re-read ALM and flow topics — both were flagged Major.
  • Use PL-400-era practice questions only for carried-over areas.

If you are starting fresh

  • Build Dataverse fundamentals first (tables, security, solutions) — the exam assumes them.
  • Follow the domain order in this guide, but do hands-on labs for each skill group; the exam rewards applied knowledge.
  • Treat Domain 3 (35–40%) as the core: plug-ins, platform APIs, flows, Azure Functions, Foundry agents.
  • Allow the full 6-week plan (see Study plan).
Microsoft's own pages lag the exam At the time of writing, the certification page still lists the old PL-400 skill-area names and says learning paths are "not yet available"; the study guide's practice-assessment link still points to the PL-400 assessment. Use the study guide's skills list (reproduced in the Skills checklist at the end of this guide) as the source of truth and fill the new-topic gaps from product documentation.

sections.title: 1.1 Design the technical architecture
sections.html:
Skills measured: identify solution components and approach • design authentication and authorization • out-of-the-box vs custom • where to implement business logic • standard / virtual / elastic tables or connectors • security-feature impact (Managed Environments, data policies, roles, teams, business units, row sharing) • deterministic vs non-deterministic logic • UX option choice • Foundry vs Copilot Studio.

Identify components and the implementation approach

  • A solution is the container for almost every customizable component: tables, columns, forms, views, apps, flows, plug-in assemblies/packages, custom APIs, connectors, environment variables, connection references. Components nest (a table owns its columns, forms, views, business rules). A solution file is limited to about 95 MB.
  • Think in three layers: the Power Platform layer (apps, Dataverse, plug-ins, flows), the Azure layer (Functions, Service Bus, Key Vault, Application Insights, managed identity) and the external system. Also account for environments, data location, platform limits and the availability/DR story.

Authentication and authorization design — which identity for which scenario

ScenarioIdentity pattern
Interactive custom app calling Dataverse as the signed-in userEntra app registration + delegated permission (Dynamics CRM user_impersonation), authorization-code flow, MSAL
Unattended service / integrationApplication user (linked to an Entra app registration) with a security role; client credentials with a certificate (or secret); scope https://{org}.crm.dynamics.com/.default
Azure Function / Azure resource calling DataverseManaged identity → application user created from the identity's application (client) ID (no secrets)
Dataverse plug-in calling an Azure resourcePower Platform managed identity for plug-ins (federated credential, signed plug-in)
Cloud flow using Dataverse without a personDataverse connection with service principal (application user + role)
CI/CD, Pipelines, Build ToolsService principal (or workload identity federation) — never a personal account
Agent reading Microsoft 365 data on behalf of a userOn-behalf-of (OBO) with the user's identity (Work IQ)
  • An application user is an unlicensed, non-interactive Dataverse user created from an Entra app registration (or a managed identity's application ID). One per app per environment. It does nothing until you assign a security role; in multi-tenant ISV scenarios the role ships in the managed solution (the app-user record itself can't).
  • pac admin create-service-principal creates the Entra app and registers it with Power Platform in one step.
  • To limit what automation can do, restrict the Dataverse security role of the application user — not the app registration.

Out-of-the-box first, then where to put the logic

The exam rewards reaching for code last: business rules, calculated/rollup/formula columns, views, charts, security roles and standard automation before plug-ins or custom UI.

RequirementBest fit
Show/hide, require, set defaults on a form (no code)Business rules
Derived valuesCalculated / rollup / formula columns
UI-reactive logic with the Client APIClient script (JavaScript/TypeScript web resource) — not trusted for security
Rich, reusable, data-bound controlPCF code component
Server-trusted validation/enforcement on every data change, any entry pointPlug-in (sync for validation, async for heavier work)
Reusable server operation with a contract callable from apps, flows and codeCustom API
Low-code, human-in-the-loop, longer-running orchestration across connectorsCloud flow (or agent flow when an agent calls it)
Long-running, heavy, scheduled or externally-triggered computeAzure Function (called from a flow/webhook/Service Bus)
Expose an external REST API to apps/flows/agentsCustom connector (+ custom code if reshaping is needed)

Standard, virtual or elastic tables — or just a connector?

TypeStorage / traitsChoose when
StandardDataverse (relational): relationships, joins, transactions, full plug-in pipeline, security modelDefault; you need relational integrity and rich logic
ElasticAzure Cosmos DB behind Dataverse: horizontal scale, flexible schema, TTL auto-delete (ttlinseconds), partitionid (20 GB per logical partition); session-level consistency (MSCRM.SessionToken); no multi-record transactions, no deep insert; CreateMultiple/UpdateMultiple/DeleteMultiple for throughputVery high volume, bursty, telemetry/log/IoT-style data, tens of millions of rows
VirtualData stays in an external system (OData v4 provider, custom provider, or no-code connector-based providers: SQL Server, SharePoint, Fabric, Salesforce, Oracle, Snowflake, PostgreSQL, Databricks); rows look nativeYou need live external data without copying it; a system of record that must stay authoritative elsewhere
Connector (no table)No Dataverse row, security, relate or Advanced Find semanticsOccasional sync/orchestration, or the source isn't available as a virtual table

Security features and their impact on solution components

  • Security roles grant privileges (Create, Read, Write, Delete, Append, Append To, Assign, Share) at an access level: None, User, Business Unit, Parent: Child Business Unit, Organization. Access is cumulative across roles. A role can hide a table your plug-in or flow needs — test with the intended identity.
  • Business units form a hierarchy; ownership can cross BUs with the matrix model (record ownership across business units). Teams: owner teams own records and hold roles; access teams never own records or hold roles and grant access through row sharing; Entra group teams sync membership from a security group.
  • Row sharing (stored in the PrincipalObjectAccess table) is an exception mechanism: it carries a performance cost and is harder to troubleshoot than roles/teams. Also know hierarchy security (manager or position) and column-level security (column security profiles; requires record access first).
  • Managed Environments (a licensing entitlement; not included in the Developer Plan) add environment groups, sharing limits, solution-checker enforcement (None / Warn / Block), usage insights, Pipelines, IP firewall, customer-managed keys, Application Insights export and alerts.
  • Data policies (DLP): connectors are Business, Non-Business (default) or Blocked; a resource can't mix Business and Non-Business connectors; the most restrictive combination wins. Nonblockable connectors (e.g., Dataverse) can be further restricted with Advanced connector policies. Custom connectors are classified by name (environment level) or host URL pattern (tenant level). Connector endpoint filtering is Preview. A data policy can silently stop a flow or app from saving/running — the first thing to check when a connector "stopped working".

Deterministic vs non-deterministic logic New

DeterministicNon-deterministic (AI)
BehaviorThe same input always gives the same outputOutput varies; model judgment
ExamplesPlug-ins, business rules, cloud flows, agent flows, topics, MCP tools, calculations, validation, approvalsAn agent reasoning over a prompt, free-text interpretation, summarization, classification, choosing which tool to call
Use forAnything auditable, reproducible or defensible (compliance, exact counts, money)Interpretation and judgment where variance is acceptable

Microsoft's agent-architecture guidance splits any solution into Input → Transform → Output and lets you choose each stage independently: unstructured (knowledge, generative models/responses) or deterministic (connectors/MCP tools, flows/code, adaptive cards/topics). A single agent usually combines both: model reasoning decides which action; deterministic tools and workflows perform it. "Deterministic" doesn't mean "no AI involved" — agent flows can be AI-assisted to build but are deterministic to run.

Foundry or Copilot Studio?

No single Microsoft page compares the two side by side — this table is a synthesis of each product's own documentation. They integrate: Copilot Studio can call Foundry agents; custom/Foundry code can consume Copilot Studio agents through the client library; both can use Power Platform MCP servers.

sections.title: 1.2 Design solution components
sections.html:
Skills measured: reusable components (generative pages, PCF, client scripting) • custom connectors and MCP servers • Dataverse code components (plug-ins, custom APIs) • automations (cloud flows, Copilot Studio workflows) • inbound/outbound integrations • custom interfaces with code apps • custom agents • monitoring and alerting.

Reusable UI components

  • PCF component: three parts — manifest, TypeScript implementation, resources; the same definition works in model-driven and canvas apps (canvas embeds a copy per app, so versions can diverge). Reuse = one packaged component consumed in many forms/apps.
  • Generative page: React code stored as a solution-aware component; add it as a Display component on a form (it receives recordId) or navigate with Xrm.Navigation.navigateTo (parameters recordId, entityName, data). Two authoring paths: AI code-generation tools (GitHub Copilot CLI/Claude Code, code-first, deploy with PAC CLI) or the in-browser maker experience.
  • Client scripting: one shared JavaScript web resource referenced from many handlers; only the documented Client API (no Xrm.Internal, no jQuery).

Custom connectors and MCP servers

  • Custom connector when apps/flows/agents must call a REST API that has no certified connector. Reshape payloads with policy templates first, custom code only when needed (1 MB, 2 minutes, one script). Put it in a solution; classify it in data policies by name/host URL (§4.3).
  • MCP server when an agent needs a tool surface. Build it with an official MCP SDK in any language, host it somewhere reachable over HTTPS (Azure Functions or Container Apps are common), use Streamable HTTP (SSE is deprecated), pick API key or OAuth 2.0, and register it in Copilot Studio through the MCP wizard or a custom connector whose OpenAPI has x-ms-agentic-protocol: mcp-streamable-1.0. Prefer Microsoft's own Dataverse MCP server (§3.5) over building one for plain Dataverse access.
  • Design choice: expose deterministic tools (specific, typed, least-privilege operations) rather than a single "do anything" tool; keep destructive operations behind approval.

Dataverse code components: plug-ins and custom APIs

  • Plug-in for server-trusted logic on data events (sync = validate/block/same transaction; async = heavier or external work). Custom API for a reusable, typed operation with request/response contract, optional privilege and (via a catalog assignment) a business event. Keep plug-ins stateless, filtered, fast (§3.1). Long-running work → Azure Function.

Automations

  • Cloud flows for general low-code automation (shareable, co-ownable, run-only users, Power Automate licensing). Copilot Studio agent flows when an agent must call deterministic business logic (consumption billing, not shareable/co-ownable). Copilot Studio workflows for the GitHub Copilot harness's visual orchestration. Pick Copilot Studio workflows/flows only when the logic is intrinsic to the agent (§3.4).

Inbound and outbound integrations with Azure

Direction / needPattern
Outbound, lightweight HTTP, sync or asyncWebhook to an Azure Function / API
Outbound, guaranteed delivery, decoupled, burstyAzure Service Bus queue (topic for several subscribers) — async only
Outbound, high-throughput streaming/telemetryAzure Event Hubs
Outbound, discoverable and low-codeBusiness events / Power Automate triggers
Inbound writes/reads from external systemsWeb API / Organization service with an application user (alternate keys + upsert, retry for 429)
Inbound, live external data surfaced in DataverseVirtual table
Long-running/scheduled processingAzure Functions (timer, Service Bus, HTTP, Durable) with managed identity

Custom interfaces with code apps

Choose a code app when the requirement is a full front-end application (your framework, your component library, custom routing, full UI control) that must still run on Power Platform with Entra sign-in, connectors and governance. Rule out a code app when you need Power Platform Git integration, SharePoint-form integration, Power Apps for Windows, IP restriction via SAS (use Conditional Access instead) or a metadata-driven UI that a model-driven app already provides (§2.3–2.4).

Custom agents that integrate with Power Platform

  • An agent needs a route in (an MCP server or connector tools), a governed identity and a place for a human to see what it did. Options: a Copilot Studio agent with Dataverse/Power Apps MCP tools and connectors; a Foundry agent calling the Dataverse MCP server and consuming Copilot Studio agents through the client library; reading Microsoft 365 context through Work IQ.
  • Dataverse security applies to MCP tool calls (no separate MCP ACL); admins allow-list MCP clients per environment (§3.5).

sections.title: 1.3 Implement application lifecycle management (ALM)
sections.html:
Skills measured: manage solution dependencies • create and use environment variables • manage solution layers • implement and extend Microsoft Power Platform Pipelines • create CI/CD automations by using Power Platform Build Tools.

Managed vs unmanaged, patches and upgrades

  • Unmanaged = development/source (editable, exportable as managed or unmanaged). Managed = the deployable artifact: can't be edited directly, can't be re-exported, deleting it removes its customizations. Develop unmanaged; deploy managed.
  • Patch = only the changes, layered on the parent, can't delete components (Microsoft doesn't recommend patches). Upgrade = rolls everything into a new base and deletes components no longer present. Stage for upgrade imports the new version beside the old (deferring deletion for a data-migration window); Apply solution upgrade then removes the old version.
  • The publisher prefix prevents naming collisions and can't change once set in a managed solution. Managed properties (set while unmanaged) lock customizability downstream.

Solution dependencies

  • Solution-level: a dependent managed solution can't be installed until its base is installed, and the base can't be uninstalled while a dependent exists (remove dependents first).
  • Component-level: internal dependencies (a form on its table) cascade automatically; published dependencies (a lookup column used on a form) must be removed by editing the component and publishing. The Show dependencies command lists dependent and required components. Messages: RetrieveDependentComponents, RetrieveRequiredComponents, RetrieveDependenciesForDelete, RetrieveDependenciesForUninstall.
  • If an unmanaged layer depends on a managed component, remove that dependency before the managed solution can be uninstalled.

Environment variables and connection references

TypesDecimal number, Text, JSON, Two options, Data source (connector + parameter info, not the connection itself), Secret (stored in Azure Key Vault)
Default value vs Current valueDefault ships in the solution definition; Current value is an environment-specific record that always wins when present. Values export as separate JSON and are edited in a deployment settings file for build tools. A client secret stored as Text is unencrypted — use the Secret type.
Connection referencesSolution components that bind a flow/app to a connection so the same solution deploys to different environments. Cloud flows use connection references for every connector; canvas apps only for implicitly-shared non-OAuth connections (e.g., SQL authentication). Code apps can bind data sources to connection references and to environment variables with @envvar:.

Solution layers

  • One unmanaged layer (all unmanaged customizations) sits above a stack of managed layers (newest on top; the system layer is the base). Only model-driven app, form and site map components merge; everything else is top wins.
  • "My customization isn't taking effect" → look at the component's Solution layers view: an unmanaged layer on top usually overrides the managed one. Fix with Remove active customizations (irreversible; removes the top unmanaged layer; if it's the only layer, delete the component instead). Editing a managed component by adding it to an unmanaged solution creates an unmanaged layer that blocks uninstalling the managed solution.
  • Segmented solutions: when adding an existing table, choose No objects (minimal, default), Edit objects (specific columns/forms), Include table metadata or Include all objects (irreversible; avoid on shared tables).

Power Platform Pipelines — implement and extend

  • A host environment stores pipelines; each pipeline has development environment(s) and ordered stages mapping to target environments (targets other than the host must be Managed Environments). Deployments follow the stage order; makers request deployment from the dev environment.
  • Only admin-hosted pipelines can be extended; personal pipelines created by makers can't.
  • Extending: three gated extension settings — Pre-export step required (first stage only), Is delegated deployment (runs as a service principal or the stage owner), Pre-deployment step required — surface Dataverse business events as Power Automate triggers (Dataverse connector → When an action is performed):
Gated extensionStarted triggerCompleted triggerFlow reports back with
Pre-export step requiredOnDeploymentRequested—UpdatePreExportStepStatus
Is delegated deploymentOnApprovalStartedOnDeploymentCompleted(connection runs as the service principal / stage owner)
Pre-deployment step requiredOnPreDeploymentStartedOnPreDeploymentCompletedUpdatePreDeploymentStepStatus
  • Other exposed events: OnApprovalCompleted, OnDeploymentStarted. Step status codes: 10 pending, 20 complete, 30 rejected (approval gates). Delegated deployment with a service principal needs the SP added as an S2S application user in the host and every target, with Deployment Pipeline Administrator (host) and System Administrator (targets).
  • CLI: pac pipeline list and pac pipeline deploy --solutionName ... --stageId ... --currentVersion ... --newVersion ....

CI/CD with Power Platform Build Tools

  • Azure DevOps extension (v2 is PAC CLI-based; don't mix task versions in one pipeline). Power Platform Tool Installer must run first. Tasks include WhoAmI, Checker (solution checker; outputs SARIF; runs on the exported solution file), Export Solution, Unpack, Pack, Import Solution (supports a holding solution for a later Apply Solution Upgrade task, and asynchronous import for large solutions), Publish Customizations, Set Solution Version, Delete Solution, plus environment-management tasks (Create/Copy/Backup/Restore/Delete/Reset — these overwrite existing service connections).
  • Standard flow: Export → Unpack (to source control) → later Pack → Import. Authenticate with a service connection (service principal is the documented preference). Supply connection references and environment variable values with a deployment settings file.
  • GitHub Actions (microsoft/powerplatform-actions): actions-install (first), whoAmI, export-solution, import-solution, pack-solution, unpack-solution; auth with app-id/client-secret/tenant-id secrets or OIDC federated credentials.
  • pac solution commands: init, clone, export, import, pack, unpack, sync, check, version, online-version, upgrade, publish, delete, list, create-settings, add-reference, add-solution-component, add-license.
Exam traps for Domain 1
  • Upgrade deletes removed components immediately; Stage for upgrade defers deletion. Patches can't delete.
  • Current value beats Default value. Secrets belong in the Secret type (Key Vault), not Text.
  • Flows always use connection references; canvas apps only for non-OAuth implicit connections.
  • Only admin-hosted pipelines are extensible; pipeline targets must be Managed Environments.
  • Advanced connector policies can't yet govern custom/HTTP/virtual connectors — keep classic data policies for those.
  • Elastic tables trade relationship/transaction parity for scale and TTL — wrong when relational integrity is required.
  • Generative pages: core GA, specific sub-features Preview. MCP widgets: M365 Copilot Chat GA, Power Apps Preview.

Sources: learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/ — admin/wp-security-cds, admin/managed-environment-overview, admin/dlp-connector-classification, admin/monitoring/alerts, alm/solution-concepts-alm, alm/solution-layers-alm, alm/pipelines, alm/extend-pipelines, alm/devops-build-tools, alm/devops-github-actions; /power-apps/maker/data-platform/ (elastic tables, environment variables, virtual tables); /power-apps/maker/model-driven-apps/generative-pages; /training/paths/design-deliver-power-platform-solutions/.

sections.title: 2.1 Apply business logic in model-driven apps by using client scripting
sections.html:
Skills measured: build code that targets the Client API object model • determine an event handler registration approach • create client scripting that targets the Dataverse Web API • configure commands and buttons by using Power Fx and JavaScript • implement navigation, dialogs, and notifications by using the Client API.

The Client API object model

  • Four roots: the execution context (passed to your handler), the form context (executionContext.getFormContext()), the grid context, and the global Xrm object. Only the documented Client API is supported — Xrm.Internal and DOM scraping can break without notice, and jQuery must not be used in form scripts.
  • formContext.data (entity, attributes, process) and formContext.ui (controls, tabs, formSelector, navigation, process, quickForms). Shortcuts: formContext.getAttribute(name), formContext.getControl(name). formContext.data.entity: getId(), getEntityName(), save(), isValid(), getIsDirty(), addOnSave().
  • executionContext.getFormContext() returns a form context or an editable-grid context depending on where it is called, so one function can serve both. Do not cache the context across await/.then()/setTimeout.
  • Xrm.Page is deprecated (v9.0) but still works; Microsoft promises at least six months' notice before removal. Use the form context and Xrm.Utility.getGlobalContext().
  • Classic ribbon trap: classic ribbon JavaScript gets no execution context — <CrmParameter Value="PrimaryControl"/> passes the form context object itself, and SelectedControl passes the grid context.
function onCreditLimitChange(executionContext) {
  const formContext = executionContext.getFormContext();
  const limit = formContext.getAttribute("creditlimit").getValue();
  const control = formContext.getControl("creditlimit");
  if (limit > 100000) control.setNotification("Limits above 100,000 need approval.", "limit-warning");
  else control.clearNotification("limit-warning");
}

Event handler registration

Static (designer)Dynamic (code)
HowForm designer → Events: library + function + "Pass execution context as the first parameter" + Enabledattribute.addOnChange, entity.addOnSave / addOnPostSave, ui.addOnLoad, lookup addPreSearch + addCustomFilter
Use whenThe logic must always run on that form; discoverable and supportable in the solutionConditional wiring (by role/state), or events with no designer surface (PreSearch, custom lookup filters, grid cells)
  • Registrable events: OnLoad, OnSave (form), TabStateChange (tab), OnChange (column), OnReadyStateComplete (IFRAME). Up to 50 handlers per element.
  • Handlers don't run in bulk-edit forms unless you set BehaviorInBulkEditForm="Enabled" in the form XML (currently for OnLoad).
  • Async OnSave: a handler that returns a Promise makes the save asynchronous; each promise has a 10-second timeout (cumulative across handlers). getEventArgs().preventDefault() cancels the save; preventDefaultOnError() cancels on a script error, rejected promise or timeout; disableAsyncTimeout() removes the timeout. getSaveMode() codes include 1 Save, 2 Save and Close, 59 Save and New, 70 AutoSave.

Calling the Dataverse Web API from client script

Use Xrm.WebApi (.online / .offline): you never build an authenticated request yourself. Methods: createRecord, retrieveRecord, retrieveMultipleRecords, updateRecord, deleteRecord, execute, executeMultiple (isAvailableOffline for offline).

  • retrieveMultipleRecords(entityLogicalName, options, maxPageSize) takes OData options ($select/$filter/$top/$expand/$orderby, URL-encoded) or a fetchXml string. Page size default/max is 5,000 (standard tables) and 500 (elastic tables); follow nextLink for more rows.
  • execute needs a request object with a getMetadata() method (boundParameter, operationName, operationType: 0 action, 1 function, 2 CRUD, parameterTypes).
  • executeMultiple: up to 1,000 requests; wrapping requests in an inner array makes a transactional change set; read operations cannot be inside a change set.
const result = await Xrm.WebApi.retrieveMultipleRecords("account", "?$select=name,creditlimit&$filter=creditlimit gt 50000&$top=10");
await Xrm.WebApi.updateRecord("account", accountId, { creditlimit: 75000 });

const whoAmI = { getMetadata: () => ({ boundParameter: null, parameterTypes: {}, operationType: 1, operationName: "WhoAmI" }) };
const data = await (await Xrm.WebApi.online.execute(whoAmI)).json();

Commands and buttons with Power Fx and JavaScript

  • Modern commanding (GA): use the in-product Command Designer (not Ribbon Workbench, which is a community tool). The first time you design commands for an app you choose JavaScript only or Power Fx; the same JavaScript library works with both. Commands are app-, table- or global-scoped and follow normal solution layering/ALM.
  • Power Fx commands run formulas over the context: Self.Selected.Item (record), Self.Selected.AllItems (table), Self.State (Edit/New/View), with functions such as Patch, Notify, Navigate. Dataverse is the data source supported for Power Fx commands.
  • Visibility is Show or Show on condition from formula — a single declarative expression that replaces most classic visibility rules.
  • JavaScript commands pass parameters such as PrimaryControl (the form context on forms) and SelectedControl (the grid). One command calls one function from one library.
  • Limits: modern commands can't build dynamic flyouts from code (classic ribbon can) and can't customize the global header.

Navigation, dialogs and notifications

APIUse forNotes
Xrm.Navigation.openForm(options, params)Open a record/new record, quick createSuccess callback fires only for quick-create saves. Cannot open a main form as a dialog.
Xrm.Navigation.navigateTo(pageInput, navOptions)Open custom pages, entity lists/records, web resources inline or as a dialogtarget: 2 = dialog; this is the way to show a main form as a modal dialog.
openAlertDialog / openConfirmDialog / openErrorDialogMessage boxesopenConfirmDialog resolves to { confirmed: boolean }. Replace deprecated Xrm.Utility.alertDialog/confirmDialog.
openUrl, openFile, openWebResourceExternal URL, file download, web resourcegetBarcodeValue/getCurrentPosition moved to Xrm.Device.
Xrm.Utility.showProgressIndicator(msg) / closeProgressIndicator()Block the UI during long workAlways close it, even on error.
NotificationAPIBlocks save?
Control (red X on a field)control.setNotification(msg, id) / clearNotification(id)Yes (control must be visible so the user can fix it)
Form bannerformContext.ui.setFormNotification(msg, "ERROR"|"WARNING"|"INFO", id) / clearFormNotification(id)No
App-level toastXrm.App.addGlobalNotification / clearGlobalNotificationNo
Exam traps
  • "Use the current best practice" + an answer using Xrm.Page → wrong; use executionContext.getFormContext().
  • Show a main form in a dialog → navigateTo, not openForm.
  • Prevent the user from saving while showing a message on a field → control.setNotification; setFormNotification alone doesn't block the save.
  • retrieveMultipleRecords page size 5,000/500 vs executeMultiple batch 1,000 — don't mix them up.

Sources: learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/model-driven-apps/clientapi/ (execution context, form context, Xrm.WebApi, Xrm.Navigation, Xrm.Utility, notifications) and /power-apps/maker/model-driven-apps/ (command designer, configure event handlers).

sections.title: 2.2 Create PCF code components
sections.html:
Skills measured: demonstrate the use of the different lifecycle events • configure a code component manifest • implement component interfaces • package, deploy, and consume a component • configure and use Device, Utility, and Web API features in component logic.

What PCF is for

A code component is a reusable control (field, dataset/grid, or view replacement) built with TypeScript/HTML/CSS and rendered in the same context and at the same time as other form components — unlike an HTML web resource in an IFRAME. It works in model-driven apps, canvas apps and (standard controls only) Power Pages, and has device, Web API and platform-dialog access that web resources lack. Don't confuse it with a code app, which is a whole standalone application.

Lifecycle — the most reliably tested topic

MethodWhen it runsWhat to do / not do
init(context, notifyOutputChanged, state, container)Once, when the component loadsBuild the DOM in container, keep references, request data/metadata. state = what context.mode.setControlState saved earlier. Call context.mode.trackContainerResize(true) here if you use allocatedWidth/Height. Dataset values aren't available yet.
updateView(context)Whenever any bound/input property, dataset, container size, offline state or label/visibility changesRe-render from context.parameters.<name>. Values can be null before the data is ready — handle that. Read datasets here.
getOutputs()After you call notifyOutputChanged()Return an object keyed by manifest properties with usage="bound" (or output) — only the changed values.
destroy()When the component is removedRemove listeners, close sockets/timers; with React, unmount.
  • A component must stay host-agnostic: it cannot use formContext directly. It communicates through bound properties (notifyOutputChanged / getOutputs); the documented workaround for form logic is an OnChange handler on the bound column.
  • Performance: batch notifyOutputChanged (e.g., on blur, not each keystroke), avoid needless dataset refresh(), never touch the host DOM outside your container, and don't call undocumented internals.

Component interfaces: standard vs virtual (React)

StandardVirtual (React)
InterfaceComponentFramework.StandardControl<IInputs, IOutputs>ComponentFramework.ReactControl<IInputs, IOutputs>
Manifestcontrol-type="standard"control-type="virtual" + <platform-library name="React" /> and/or Fluent
initHas a container parameter — you manipulate the DOMNo container; updateView returns a ReactElement
HostsModel-driven, canvas, Power PagesModel-driven and canvas — not Power Pages
Scaffoldpac pcf init --framework nonepac pcf init --framework react (an existing standard control can't be converted)
  • IInputs/IOutputs are generated from the manifest into ManifestTypes.d.ts; read bound values with context.parameters.<property>.
  • React and Fluent are platform libraries (shared, not bundled): smaller bundle.js, one copy per app. use platform libraries or bundle your own — don't mix. Fluent 8 and Fluent 9 can't both be declared in one manifest; use PAC CLI ≥ 1.37.

The manifest (ControlManifest.Input.xml)

<manifest>
  <control namespace="Contoso" constructor="StarRating" version="1.0.0"
           display-name-key="StarRating_Display" description-key="StarRating_Desc" control-type="standard">
    <property name="value"    display-name-key="Value"     of-type="Whole.None" usage="bound" required="true" />
    <property name="maxStars" display-name-key="Max stars" of-type="Whole.None" usage="input" default-value="5" />
    <resources>
      <code path="index.ts" order="1" />
      <css  path="css/StarRating.css" order="1" />
      <resx path="strings/StarRating.1033.resx" version="1.0.0" />
    </resources>
    <feature-usage>
      <uses-feature name="WebAPI" required="true" />
      <uses-feature name="Device.getCurrentPosition" required="false" />
    </feature-usage>
  </control>
</manifest>
  • control: namespace, constructor (class name), version, display-name-key, description-key, control-type. The build output renames the file to ControlManifest.xml.
  • property: name, display-name-key, of-type or of-type-group (+ a type-group element), usage = bound | input | output, required, default-value.
  • data-set (dataset components; model-driven only; primary dataset property is named Items). resources is required and must contain at least one code element (also css, img, resx, platform-library, dependency).
  • external-service-usage (canvas apps): with enabled="true" and a <domain>, the component becomes premium (users need a Power Apps license).

Device, Utility and Web API features

FeatureDeclare in feature-usageUse in codeWhere available
DeviceDevice.captureAudio / captureImage / captureVideo / getBarcodeValue / getCurrentPosition / pickFilecontext.device.captureImage(options), getCurrentPosition(), …Model-driven and canvas; not Power Pages
UtilityUtilitycontext.utils.getEntityMetadata, hasEntityPrivilege, lookupObjectsModel-driven only
Web APIWebAPIcontext.webAPI.createRecord / retrieveRecord / retrieveMultipleRecords / updateRecord / deleteRecordModel-driven and Power Pages — not canvas
Exam trap — required flag required="true" + a host that doesn't support the feature → the component fails to load at runtime. required="false" → the API is simply null and you check it in code. With no uses-feature element the API is null everywhere. (Microsoft's pages vary the casing of the Device. prefix; follow the documented sample.)

Other context members: context.mode (allocatedHeight/Width, isControlDisabled, isVisible, label, setControlState, setFullScreen, trackContainerResize), context.navigation, context.formatting, context.resources, context.userSettings.

Develop, package, deploy and consume

pac auth create --environment <env-url-or-id>
pac pcf init --namespace Contoso --name StarRating --template field --framework none --run-npm-install
npm start watch          # local test harness with hot reload (mock data)
npm run build            # build in RELEASE mode for deployment (dev builds are larger and may be rejected on import)
pac pcf push --publisher-prefix contoso    # fast dev path: deploys to a temporary PowerAppsTools_contoso solution
  • Two project types: .pcfproj = one component; .cdsproj = solution project that can reference many. Release path: pac solution init → pac solution add-reference --path <pcfproj> → build with msbuild /restore / dotnet build → import the solution (manually or via Build Tools). pac pcf version bumps versions.
  • pac pcf push options: --publisher-prefix (2–8 characters, can't start with mscrm), --solution-unique-name, --environment, --incremental.
  • Consume: model-driven — add to a form field/section or replace a grid/view (enabled by default). Canvas — an admin must enable Power Apps component framework for canvas apps for the environment (Settings → Product → Features); a copy is embedded in each app, so two apps can run different versions and the maker accepts an "Update code components" prompt. Power Pages — standard controls with a limited set of field types.
  • Debug after deployment: Fiddler AutoResponder (or Requestly) maps the deployed bundle.js to your local build; browser DevTools; the test harness uses mock data. TypeScript target defaults to ES5.

Sources: learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/component-framework/ — overview, custom-controls-overview, manifest-schema-reference/*, reference/*, import-custom-controls, implementing-controls-using-typescript, react-controls-platform-libraries.

sections.title: 2.3 Build Power Apps code apps
sections.html:
Skills measured: configure code apps to use Power Platform connections • use Dataverse tables • perform table and metadata operations • perform Dataverse actions and functions • use Power Automate cloud flows • use Copilot Studio agents • use environment variables. (Also Domain 1: design custom interfaces by using code apps.)

What a code app is

A code app is a custom single-page web app (React, Vue or any framework) that you build in a code-first IDE such as VS Code and that runs natively inside Power Apps: Microsoft Entra authentication, 1,500+ connectors and Dataverse callable from JavaScript/TypeScript, hosting in Power Platform, and the platform's governance (sharing limits, Conditional Access, data policies) and ALM. Code apps are generally available.

OptionChoose it when…Code apps differ because…
Canvas appLow-code, Power Fx, maker-built UIYou write 100% of the UI and logic in your own framework and build pipeline
Model-driven appMetadata-driven Dataverse forms/viewsNo generated UI; you call generated services yourself
PCF componentA reusable control inside a form or canvas screenA code app is a standalone, separately shared app with its own play URL
Power PagesExternal/anonymous sitesCode apps always authenticate with Entra ID — internal/B2B line-of-business use

Runtime = your code + the Power Apps SDK (@microsoft/power-apps, with generated models/services) + the Power Apps host (authentication, loading, error UI). Project metadata (connections, data sources, app settings) lives in the generated power.config.json.

Prerequisites and licensing

  • Tools: an IDE (VS Code), Node.js LTS, Git, the Power Apps CLI.
  • An admin must enable code apps per environment: Power Platform admin center → Manage → Environments → (env) → Settings → Product → Features → Enable code apps. Can be set at scale with environment groups and rules.
  • End users need Power Apps Premium, pay-as-you-go, an App Pass, or auto-claim.
  • A Managed Environment is not a stated prerequisite, but code apps honor Managed Environment policies (sharing limits, Conditional Access, data policy enforcement at launch) when you configure them.
Exam trap — two CLIs The current, generally available tool is the standalone Power Apps CLI: pa (npm package @microsoft/power-apps-cli). The older pac code ... commands (pac code init, pac code push, pac code add-data-source) are Preview/legacy and documented as being replaced. Unless a question explicitly says "classic pac CLI", the pa app ... syntax is the right answer.

The build → run → publish loop

npx degit github:microsoft/PowerAppsCodeApps/templates/vite my-app   # or templates/starter (React + Vite + Tailwind + TanStack)
cd my-app
npm install --global @microsoft/power-apps-cli
npm install --global @microsoft/power-apps
npm install
pa app init --display-name "Contoso Orders" --environment-id <environment-id>   # binds project to an environment
pa app run          # starts the local host; open the "Local Play" URL in the SAME browser profile as your tenant
npm run build
pa app push         # publishes the compiled app and returns its Power Apps URL

pa app init options: --display-name, --environment-id, --description, --build-path (default ./dist), --file-entry-point (default index.html), --app-type CodeApp|MobileApp, --app-url, --cloud. Local Play can fail because Chrome/Edge block public-origin → localhost requests ("local network access"): grant the permission, or add allow="local-network-access" to an embedding iframe.

Power Apps CLI (pa) commandPurpose
pa auth login | logout | status | switchSign in and manage accounts
pa connector list • pa connection create | list | list-datasets | list-tables | list-procedures | list-referencesDiscover connectors; create/list connections and their datasets, tables, SQL procedures, connection references
pa app init | run | push | list | share | get-settings | set-settingCreate/bind, local-run, publish, list, share, and configure the app
pa app add data-source • pa app remove data-source • pa app refresh data-sourceConnectors and tables (Dataverse included) → generated model/service files
pa app find-dataverse-api --search • pa app add dataverse-api --api-nameFind/add Dataverse actions and functions
pa app list-flows • pa app add flow --flow-id • pa app remove flowSolution-aware cloud flows
pa app list-environment-variablesSolution environment variables available to the app
pa solution list • pa telemetry enable | disable | statusFind solutions; CLI telemetry

Connections and connectors (skill: configure code apps to use Power Platform connections)

  • Flow: pa connector list → pa connection create --connector <id> → pa app add data-source --connector <id> .... Connector IDs look like shared_office365users; a display name also works.
  • Use --connection-id for a direct connection, or --connection-ref + --solution-id to bind through a connection reference (solution-aware, portable across environments).
  • Connectors that offer both tables and actions (SharePoint, SQL Server) need --as table or --as action; action-only connectors (Office 365 Users) don't. Repeat --table to add several tables from the same connector/connection/dataset. A SQL stored procedure uses --procedure.
  • Not supported: Excel Online (Business) and Excel Online (OneDrive) connectors.

Dataverse tables and CRUD (skill: configure code apps to use Dataverse tables)

pa app add data-source --connector dataverse --table account    # native Dataverse: ONE table per command; no connection ID/dataset

This generates src/generated/models/AccountsModel.ts and src/generated/services/AccountsService.ts. Service methods: create, get, getAll, update, delete (plus getMetadata).

import { AccountsService } from './generated/services/AccountsService';
import type { Accounts } from './generated/models/AccountsModel';

const created = await AccountsService.create({ name: 'New Account' } as Omit<Accounts, 'accountid'>);

const options = {                       // IGetAllOptions
  select: ['name', 'accountnumber', 'address1_city'],   // ALWAYS limit columns
  filter: "address1_country eq 'USA'",                  // OData filter string
  orderBy: ['name asc'], top: 50, maxPageSize: 50
};
const result = await AccountsService.getAll(options);    // result.data
await AccountsService.update(accountId, { telephone1: '555-0123' });
await AccountsService.delete(accountId);
  • IGetAllOptions: maxPageSize, select, filter, orderBy, top, skip, skipToken. Delegation is supported for Filter, Sort, Top; paging is supported.
  • Also supported: formatted values (option-set labels), lookups (via the Web API associate patterns), image/file upload-download (Preview), table metadata.
  • Not supported yet: polymorphic lookups, schema definition (entity metadata) CRUD, FetchXML, alternate keys.

Table and metadata operations

const { data } = await AccountsService.getMetadata({ schema: { columns: 'all' } });
const labels = data.Attributes?.map(a => [a.LogicalName, a.DisplayName?.UserLocalizedLabel?.Label]);

getMetadata(options?: GetEntityMetadataOptions) returns Partial<EntityMetadata>: Attributes, OneToManyRelationships, ManyToOneRelationships, ManyToManyRelationships. Use schema.columns ('all' or a list) and the relationship flags to control what is returned. Metadata is read-only here.

Dataverse actions and functions

pa app find-dataverse-api --search "WhoAmI"          # case-insensitive substring match; --json for machine output
pa app add dataverse-api --api-name WhoAmI           # generates WhoAmIService
  • Unbound function: WhoAmIService.WhoAmI(). Bound action: the bound record's ID is the first argument, e.g. AddToQueueService.AddToQueue(queueId, target, sourceQueue, queueItemProperties).
  • Requires @microsoft/power-apps ≥ 1.1.1. Re-run the command to refresh the generated service if the API changes. Custom APIs appear here too.

Power Automate cloud flows

pa app list-flows --search "approval"
pa app add flow --flow-id <guid>                  # generates ApprovalWorkflowService

// in your code
const result = await ApprovalWorkflowService.Run({ requester: 'Alex', amount: 1500 });  // { success, data, error }
Exam trap Only solution-aware, instant flows that use the Power Apps trigger are supported. Scheduled flows, automated flows and instant flows with other triggers are not. The maker needs access to the flow and its connections; end users need Dataverse permission to invoke it (assign the App Opener security role or an equivalent). Re-run pa app add flow after the flow definition changes.

Copilot Studio agents

pa app add data-source --connector shared_microsoftcopilotstudio --connection-id <id>

// in your code
const r = await CopilotStudioService.ExecuteCopilotAsyncV2({
  message: "What is the status of my order?",
  notificationUrl: "https://notificationurlplaceholder",
  agentName: "cr3e1_customerSupportAgent" });      // r.data: { responses[], conversationId, lastResponse, completed }
  • The agent must be published; its schema name is on Channels → Web app in Copilot Studio.
  • Use ExecuteCopilotAsyncV2. ExecuteCopilot is fire-and-forget (returns only a ConversationId) and ExecuteCopilotAsync can fail with HTTP 502 — both are distractors.

Environment variables

Two unrelated concepts share the name:

KindExamplesUse
Solution environment variables (Dataverse)--dataset "@envvar:crd1b_SharepointSiteVar" --table "@envvar:crd1b_sharepointList"Make a data source portable across environments; the reference is stored in power.config.json. List them with pa app list-environment-variables.

sections.title: 2.4 Deploy and manage Power Apps code apps
sections.html:
Skills measured: configure Content Security Policy (CSP) • implement monitoring with Azure Application Insights • package, deploy and share • troubleshoot with Monitor and browser tools • optimize performance and resource usage.

Content Security Policy (CSP)

  • Configured per environment (not per app) by an admin: Power Platform admin center → Environments → (env) → Settings → Product → Privacy + Security → Content security policy → App tab. CSP is enforced by default.
  • Custom values are appended to the defaults — except where the default is 'none', in which case your value replaces it. Enable reporting sends violation reports to your endpoint whether or not a directive is enforced.
  • Scripted alternative: Power Platform API PATCH .../environmentmanagement/environments/{id}/settings with PowerApps_CSPEnabledCodeApps, PowerApps_CSPReportingEndpoint, PowerApps_CSPConfigCodeApps.
Default directiveValueTypical reason to change it
connect-src'none'Allow your own APIs and the Application Insights ingestion endpoint
script-src'self' + platformThird-party script hosts
img-src / media-src'self' data: (+ platform for images)External images/CDNs
font-src / style-src'self' / 'self' 'unsafe-inline'External fonts or stylesheets
frame-ancestors'self' https://*.powerapps.comEmbed the code app in an iframe (e.g., a model-driven app): add the host origin. Cross-tenant iframe sharing isn't possible.
frame-src, form-action, child-src, worker-src, manifest-src'self' or 'none'Embedded content / form posts / workers
Diagnosis tip Symptom "nothing is sent to my API / telemetry is missing" + browser console error "Connecting to '...' violates the following Content Security Policy directive" → add the host to connect-src in the environment's CSP.

Monitoring with Azure Application Insights

  • Integration is manual (nothing is automatic): npm i @microsoft/applicationinsights-web, initialize with your connection string, and register the logger once with setConfig({ logger: { logMetric } }) from @microsoft/power-apps/app (the ILogger type is in @microsoft/power-apps/telemetry).
  • Built-in metric payloads: SessionLoadSummaryMetricData (successfulAppLaunch, appLoadResult, timeToAppInteractive) and NetworkRequestMetricData (url, method, duration, statusCode, responseSize).
  • Allow the App Insights ingestion endpoint in CSP connect-src or events are silently blocked. Instrumentation keys are not yet supported via environment variables — read the key from a Dataverse settings table or getContext().
  • Trap: App Insights only sees telemetry after a successful load; startup failures show up only in Power Platform Monitor.
  • Platform view (no code): Power Platform admin center → Monitor → Products → Power Apps shows code-app metrics: Time to Interactive, app session count, app open success rate, data request success rate, data request latency.

Package, deploy and share

  • pa app push [--solution-id <GUID>] [--non-interactive]. First publish picks the preferred solution, else the Default solution (no solution in non-Dataverse environments); later publishes keep the solution unless you pass --solution-id. The ID must be a GUID — solution names are rejected. In CI/CD set PA_CLI_SOLUTION_ID.
  • Add an existing app to a solution later: make.powerapps.com → Solutions → Add existing → App → Code app. Promote across stages with Power Platform Pipelines. Power Platform Git integration is not supported.
  • Share with pa app share --principal <emails/objectIds> --access play|edit (default play). Sharing limits, connector consent, quarantine and per-app Conditional Access apply.
  • Service-principal publishing in CI/CD: the app maker must first manually share edit access with the principal, and you use the Enterprise Application (service principal) object ID — not the App Registration object ID.

Troubleshoot with Monitor and browser tools

  • Open DevTools (F12): Network tab — filter apihub.net for connector traffic and dynamics.com for Dataverse traffic; inspect status codes, payloads and timings. Console → Errors shows CSP violations.
  • Power Platform Monitor for session-level KPIs and startup failures; Local Play problems are usually browser local network access blocking or the wrong browser profile, not code.
  • Permission errors on flows/Dataverse → check the user's security role (App Opener or equivalent) and connection consent.

Optimize performance and resource usage

  • Always pass select to getAll; push filter / sort / top to the server (delegation) and use paging (maxPageSize, skipToken).
  • Cache and de-duplicate requests (e.g., TanStack Query in the starter template), lazy-load routes, and keep the production bundle small (npm run build).
  • Track Time to Interactive and data request latency/success in Monitor and App Insights. (Microsoft has no separate numeric performance thresholds for code apps — treat any specific figure as unverified.)

Limitations to memorize

Not supported / doesn't applyUse instead
Storage SAS IP restriction / firewall (hosted assets are on a public endpoint)Conditional Access — block access by location (code apps use Entra ID)
Secure Implicit Connections— (not yet supported)
Power Platform Git integrationYour own Git repo; deploy with pa app push / Pipelines
Power Apps for Windows; SharePoint forms integration; native Power BI integration (PowerBIIntegration)Power Apps visual in Power BI
Excel Online connectors; polymorphic lookups; FetchXML; alternate keys; schema CRUDOther connectors / Web API patterns / maker portal

About 60% of it is classic Dataverse extensibility you may know from PL-400 (plug-ins, Web API/Organization service, Azure Functions, flows); the rest is new or reworked: managed identity for plug-ins, background operations, the Python SDK, Copilot Studio workflows and the whole Foundry agents group.

sections.title: 3.1 Create a Dataverse plug-in
sections.html:
Skills measured: event execution pipeline stages • execution context • business logic • images • Organization service • performance • custom API message • Plug-in Registration Tool • plug-in that implements a custom API • business events • managed identity for plug-ins. This is the single heaviest topic on the exam — build every item in this section at least once.

1. The event execution pipeline

Stage#What it is / when to use itTransaction
PreValidation10Runs before security/privilege checks. Cancel invalid requests cheaply before the database transaction starts.Generally outside (check IsInTransaction)
PreOperation20Before the database write. Change the Target here (set defaults, normalize values) — the changes are saved with no extra call.Inside
MainOperation30The platform's own operation. Internal-only — ISVs can't register steps here. The exception: a Custom API (or custom virtual-table data provider) linked plug-in type runs at this stage.Inside
PostOperation40After the write. Use for follow-on work: create related records, call out, publish events. Asynchronous mode is only valid here.Synchronous: inside. Asynchronous: outside
  • Mode: 0 = Synchronous, 1 = Asynchronous. Synchronous = user waits, can block/validate, participates in the transaction. Asynchronous = queued as a system job (AsyncOperation), can't roll back the operation that queued it.
  • Rollback: in a synchronous step any unhandled exception rolls back the whole transaction; InvalidPluginExecutionException additionally controls the message shown to the user. In async steps the error is recorded on the system job and nothing is shown. new InvalidPluginExecutionException(OperationStatus.Retry, ...) asks the async service to retry (up to 4 times).
  • Steps are matched on message (Create, Update, Delete, Assign, SetState, custom API names…) + primary table. Multiple steps at the same stage run by execution order (rank) — set it explicitly; ties are not guaranteed.
  • Depth guards against infinite loops: default maximum 8 calls in a 1-hour window, then the platform aborts execution. Check context.Depth in plug-ins that update their own table.

2. The execution context and the plug-in skeleton

public class SetAccountDefaults : IPlugin
{
    public void Execute(IServiceProvider serviceProvider)
    {
        var tracing = (ITracingService)serviceProvider.GetService(typeof(ITracingService));
        var context = (IPluginExecutionContext)serviceProvider.GetService(typeof(IPluginExecutionContext));
        var factory = (IOrganizationServiceFactory)serviceProvider.GetService(typeof(IOrganizationServiceFactory));
        IOrganizationService service = factory.CreateOrganizationService(context.UserId);

        if (context.MessageName != "Create" || context.Depth > 1) return;           // simple loop guard
        if (!(context.InputParameters["Target"] is Entity target)) return;            // Entity for Create/Update

        if (!target.Contains("creditlimit")) target["creditlimit"] = new Money(5000m); // PreOperation: saved with the row
        tracing.Trace("Defaults applied to {0} ({1})", context.PrimaryEntityName, context.CorrelationId);
    }
}
Context memberMeaning
MessageName, PrimaryEntityName, PrimaryEntityIdWhat is happening, to which table and row
Stage / Mode / Depth / IsInTransaction10/20/40 • 0 sync, 1 async • call depth • whether a DB transaction is active
InputParameters / OutputParametersMessage payload and results. Target is an Entity for Create/Update but an EntityReference for Delete. For Update, Target contains only the changed attributes.
PreEntityImages / PostEntityImagesRegistered snapshots (see Images)
SharedVariablesPass data between plug-ins in the same pipeline execution
UserId / InitiatingUserIdUserId = the user the step runs as (impersonated user, else the caller). InitiatingUserId = the user who actually triggered the operation.
CorrelationId, OperationId, RequestIdTracing and linking to the system job
ParentContextThe calling pipeline's context — don't depend on its ordering
  • The context interface family: IExecutionContext → IPluginExecutionContext (adds Stage, ParentContext) → IPluginExecutionContext2…7 (more members such as application IDs, images collections, EnvironmentId/TenantId, IsApplicationUser). There is no IPluginExecutionContext8.
  • Other services from the provider: IOrganizationServiceFactory, ITracingService (view output in the Plugin Trace Log), IServiceEndpointNotificationService, IManagedIdentityService, and Microsoft.Xrm.Sdk.PluginTelemetry.ILogger (Application Insights logging; not Microsoft.Extensions.Logging.ILogger).

3. Business logic patterns

GoalRegister as
Reject bad data early, before security checks and the transactionPreValidation (10) sync; throw InvalidPluginExecutionException
Validate or default values that must be saved with the rowPreOperation (20) sync; edit Target
Create/update other rows atomically with the main operationPostOperation (40) sync (same transaction → rolls back together)
Heavy, slow or external work that shouldn't block the userPostOperation (40) async (or hand off to an Azure Function)
Run only when specific columns changeSet filtering attributes on Update steps (the step fires if a listed column is present in the payload; never include the primary key)

4. Pre- and post-images

  • Registered on the step with a name and alias; read with context.PreEntityImages["alias"] / PostEntityImages["alias"]. Restrict the columns (the default of "all" is discouraged) — an image is cheaper than an extra Retrieve.
  • No pre-image on Create (the row doesn't exist yet). No post-image on Delete. Post-images are only available in PostOperation. Pre-images work in all three stages. Images apply only to messages such as Create, Update, Delete, Assign, SetState, Merge, Route, Send — not Associate/Disassociate.
  • Typical use: on Update, compare PreEntityImages["pre"]["statuscode"] with Target to detect a transition; or read a column that isn't in Target.

5. Organization service inside plug-ins

  • factory.CreateOrganizationService(userId): null = the SYSTEM user; Guid.Empty = the same user as context.UserId; any other GUID = that specific user. Common choices: context.UserId (the user the step runs as, honoring "Run in User's Context"), context.InitiatingUserId (override to the user who triggered it), or an explicit SystemUserId (that user needs the privileges).
  • IOrganizationService has eight methods: Create, Retrieve, Update, Delete, Execute, Associate, Disassociate, RetrieveMultiple. Everything else is an Execute request.
  • Avoid ExecuteMultipleRequest / ExecuteTransactionRequest and the four bulk request types (CreateMultiple…) inside plug-ins — Microsoft's best practice is "don't use batch request types in plug-ins". Writing a plug-in registered on CreateMultiple/UpdateMultiple is fine.
  • "Merged pipeline": a step registered on Create still fires once per row when a client calls CreateMultiple. You only register on CreateMultiple to get batch-level processing performance — and then you must avoid running the same logic twice.
  • Creating a row from a plug-in on a standard table in a synchronous step stays inside the transaction; on elastic tables there is no multi-record transaction, so a failure does not roll back an earlier write.

6. Optimizing plug-in performance

DoDon't
Keep the class stateless — Dataverse caches and reuses plug-in instances across threads; only const/readonly config and the constructor's secure/unsecure strings are safeStore per-call data in instance or static fields (thread-safety bugs)
Retrieve only needed columns (ColumnSet); use imagesRetrieve all columns / unbounded RetrieveMultiple (can crash the sandbox worker)
Use filtering attributes; avoid duplicate step registrations; limit Retrieve/RetrieveMultiple steps (the platform fires at least two Retrieve messages per call)Update the same row in its own PostOperation (it re-triggers the pipeline)
Keep synchronous logic short (target about 2 seconds) and move the rest to async or Azure FunctionsExceed the 2-minute limit — the operation fails and rolls back (the limit also covers async plug-ins; background operations don't extend it)
Use ITracingService/ILogger sparinglyUse threads, Task.Run/TPL or other parallel code (unsupported in the sandbox)
  • Plug-ins run in the sandbox (mandatory): approved reference assemblies only, no unmanaged code, no low-level Windows API. Outbound HTTP calls are supported (set short timeouts). The plug-in assembly itself targets .NET Framework 4.6.2–4.8 (not .NET 8), even though PAC CLI and ServiceClient have moved to modern .NET.
  • Sandbox crashes surface as "Sandbox Worker process crashed" (-2147204723) — look for unhandled exceptions, unguarded threads, runaway memory.

7. Packaging and the Plug-in Registration Tool (PRT)

pac plugin init --author Contoso            # scaffold a .NET Framework 4.6.2 class library (-sk to sign, -ss to skip signing)
dotnet build -c Release
pac tool prt                                # launch the Plug-in Registration Tool
pac plugin push --pluginId <guid> --type Nuget   # push an updated package/assembly (--type Assembly for a classic DLL)
Classic assemblyPlug-in package (NuGet, .nupkg)
DependenciesSingle DLL (ILMerge is unsupported by Microsoft)Dependent assemblies supported
SigningStrong-name signing required (and every dependency must be signed)No signing required
Limits16 MB assembly; no unmanaged codeNo workflow activities, not on-premises
  • Step fields: message, primary table, filtering attributes, event pipeline stage (PreValidation/PreOperation/PostOperation), execution mode, execution order, Run in User's Context (default Calling User), unsecure configuration (exported with the solution) and secure configuration (not exported; admin-readable; passed through the constructor MyPlugin(string unsecure, string secure)). Images: type (pre/post), name, entity alias, columns.
  • Early-bound classes (including custom API request/response helpers): pac modelbuilder build. NuGet: Microsoft.CrmSdk.CoreAssemblies.

8. Custom APIs and the plug-ins behind them

A custom API creates your own message (callable through the Web API as Microsoft.Dynamics.CRM.<UniqueName>, the SDK, flows and code apps) backed by a plug-in. It is the code-first replacement for custom process actions.

CustomAPI columnMeaning
UniqueNameImmutable, must include the publisher prefix
BindingType (+ BoundEntityLogicalName)0 Global, 1 Entity (adds a Target EntityReference parameter), 2 EntityCollection — immutable
IsFunctiontrue → OData Function (HTTP GET, no side effects, must return at least one response property); false → Action (POST). Immutable. Power Automate's Dataverse connector can call actions, not functions.
IsPrivateHides it from metadata/code generation (not security); private messages can't be a plug-in step target
AllowedCustomProcessingStepType0 None (only your plug-in), 1 AsyncOnly (others may observe via async steps; recommended for business events), 2 SyncAndAsync (others can alter/cancel)
ExecutePrivilegeNameOptional; must name an existing privilege (there's no supported way to create a new one)
PluginTypeIdThe plug-in type that runs at stage 30 — you don't register a step for it
  • Child tables: CustomAPIRequestParameter (UniqueName, Type, IsOptional, LogicalEntityName for entity types) and CustomAPIResponseProperty. Types: Boolean, DateTime, Decimal, Entity, EntityCollection, EntityReference, Float, Integer, Money, Picklist, String, StringArray, Guid (no File type).
  • Create via the Plug-in Registration Tool (the better experience), the maker portal (Solutions → New → More → Other → Custom API), raw Web API calls, or solution XML. There is no pac customapi command.
  • Custom API vs custom process action: custom API = code-first, can require a privilege, can be private, localizable, function or action, can bind to an entity collection, ALM-friendly XML; but it is subject to the 2-minute plug-in limit. Process action = designer-based, always an action.
  • Ship managed with Is Customizable = false on the API and on each parameter/property.
public class CalculateDiscount : IPlugin          // linked as the Custom API's plug-in type (PluginTypeId)
{
    public void Execute(IServiceProvider sp)
    {
        var ctx = (IPluginExecutionContext)sp.GetService(typeof(IPluginExecutionContext));
        var total = (Money)ctx.InputParameters["OrderTotal"];            // request parameter UniqueName
        ctx.OutputParameters["Discount"] = new Money(total.Value * 0.10m); // response property UniqueName
    }
}

9. Dataverse business events

  • Business events let Dataverse announce that something happened to many kinds of listeners: Power Automate flows, Azure Service Bus, Azure Event Hubs, webhooks, and Dataverse plug-ins (Event Grid is also a supported endpoint contract). They reuse the existing ServiceEndpoint table and add a discovery catalog (Catalog, CatalogAssignment).
  • Out of the box the catalog exposes Create/Update/Delete for cataloged tables, GrantAccess/ModifyAccess/RevokeAccess for user-owned tables, and OnExternalCreated/Updated/Deleted for virtual tables.
  • A custom API becomes a business event through a CatalogAssignment record (there is no "enable business event" flag on the API). A custom API with no plug-in is a pure event — useful to expose a new Power Automate trigger. Set AllowedCustomProcessingStepType to AsyncOnly for this pattern.
  • Power Automate trigger: Microsoft Dataverse → "When an action is performed" (parameters: Catalog, Category, Table name, Action name). Plain row events use "When a row is added, modified or deleted". "When a business event occurs" belongs to Finance & Operations, not Dataverse.
  • Service endpoint payload schema (SchemaType): 1 = Event Grid, 2 = Cloud Events.

10. Power Platform managed identity for plug-ins New

Lets a plug-in call Azure resources (Key Vault, Storage, Graph…) without storing a secret. Supported for plug-in assemblies and plug-in packages (documented as GA); the pac managed-identity command group is Preview.

ElementFacts
MechanismA federated identity credential (FIC) on a user-assigned managed identity or app registration trusts a token that Dataverse issues for your signed plug-in. The plug-in then exchanges it for an Entra token for the target resource.
Codevar mi = (IManagedIdentityService)serviceProvider.GetService(typeof(IManagedIdentityService)); → string token = mi.AcquireToken(new[] { "https://vault.azure.net/.default" }); (an overload takes a managedIdentityId)
SigningMandatory (signtool / nuget sign); the certificate's issuer/subject feed the FIC subject. Self-signed is for dev/test only.
FIC valuesIssuer https://login.microsoftonline.com/{tenantId}/v2.0; audience api://AzureADTokenExchange; version 2 (recommended) uses SHA-256 hashes of the certificate issuer/subject; version 1 (legacy, unhashed DN) fails with AADSTS70050 / AADSTS700213 on commas or non-ASCII characters.
Dataverse recordA managedidentity row (applicationid, tenantid, credentialsource, subjectscope, version) linked to the pluginassembly/pluginpackage via managedidentityid@odata.bind
CLI (all Preview)pac managed-identity create | get | update | delete | configure-fic | show-fic | verify-fic | upgrade-version
Setup order(1) Create the identity/app registration → (2) build, sign and register the plug-in → (3) add the federated credential in Entra → (4) create and link the managedidentity record → (5) grant the identity access to the Azure resource → (6) test/verify
Exam traps for plug-ins
  • CreateOrganizationService(null) = SYSTEM, not the calling user (Guid.Empty or context.UserId is).
  • Stage 30 is "internal-only" — except the plug-in type linked to a Custom API.
  • Async plug-in failures do not roll back the original operation. Pre-image on Create and post-image on Delete don't exist; no images for Associate/Disassociate.
  • A Create step fires under CreateMultiple; DeleteMultiple works on elastic tables only.
  • Classic assemblies need strong-name signing; plug-in packages don't — but managed identity needs the plug-in signed with a certificate either way.
  • Managed identity for plug-ins (outbound from Dataverse) ≠ an Azure Function using a managed identity to call Dataverse (§3.3). Different direction, different setup.

Sources: learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/ — plug-ins, event-framework, write-plug-in, register-plug-in, understand-the-data-context, custom-api, custom-api-tables, business-events, impersonate-a-user, best-practices/business-logic/*; /dotnet/api/microsoft.xrm.sdk.iorganizationservicefactory.createorganizationservice; /power-platform/admin/set-up-managed-identity; /power-platform/developer/cli/reference/managed-identity, /plugin.

sections.title: 3.2 Perform operations by using platform APIs
sections.html:
Skills measured: Dataverse Web API • Organization service • API-limit retry policies • optimize for performance, concurrency, transactions and bulk operations • implement and troubleshoot OAuth • asynchronous logic with background operations • Dataverse SDKs for .NET and Python.

Dataverse Web API

OData v4.0 endpoint [org URI]/api/data/v9.2/. All CRUD routes through the Organization service; other messages appear as OData functions (GET, no side effects) or actions (POST, side effects). GET /api/data/v9.2/ returns the service document (entity-set names — use the table's EntitySetName, not always the logical name + "s").

NeedHow
Select / filter / expand$select, $filter, $expand, $orderby, $top, $count
Paging$skip is NOT supported. Follow @odata.nextLink (opaque $skiptoken). Page size Prefer: odata.maxpagesize=N (max 5,000, standard and elastic tables).
FetchXMLURL-encoded ?fetchXml=<fetch>... on the entity set; null columns are omitted from results. Very long FetchXML goes in a $batch body.
Formatted values / lookup namesPrefer: odata.include-annotations="OData.Community.Display.V1.FormattedValue" (or "*")
CreatePOST to the entity set → 204 + OData-EntityId header (new GUID). Prefer: return=representation returns the body.
UpdatePATCH — send only changed properties (a full retrieved payload fires spurious change events/audit). Returns 204.
UpsertPATCH to a URL keyed by an alternate key (or ID). If-Match: * = update only (blocks the implicit create); If-None-Match: * = create only.
Optimistic concurrencyIf-Match: W/"<@odata.etag>"; stale ETag → 412 Precondition Failed.
AssociateSingle-valued: "primarycontactid@odata.bind": "/contacts(<guid>)" in the body. Collection-valued / N:N: POST .../$ref with @odata.id; disassociate with DELETE .../$ref?$id=....
Batch$batch ≤ 1,000 requests, no nesting; $batch ≈ ExecuteMultiple; a changeset inside it ≈ ExecuteTransaction (all-or-nothing).
Actions / functionsFunctions: GET, use parameter aliases (?@p1=...) for long/reserved-character values. Actions: POST with JSON body.
ImpersonationHeader CallerObjectId (Entra object ID, preferred) or legacy MSCRMCallerID (systemuserid). The caller needs prvActOnBehalfOfAnotherUser (Delegate role); effective privileges are the intersection.

Organization service (.NET)

  • IOrganizationService (Create, Retrieve, RetrieveMultiple, Update, Delete, Associate, Disassociate, Execute) is implemented by ServiceClient (Microsoft.PowerPlatform.Dataverse.Client, MSAL-based; use this) and the legacy CrmServiceClient. OrganizationServiceProxy is deprecated.
  • ExecuteMultipleRequest: up to 1,000 requests per call, ContinueOnError/ReturnResponses settings, not transactional (each request commits independently) — check IsFaulted per response.
  • ExecuteTransactionRequest: all requests succeed or all roll back; the fault reports the failing request's index.
  • Bulk messages — CreateMultiple, UpdateMultiple, UpsertMultiple (needs alternate keys), DeleteMultiple (elastic tables only). They take a Targets collection and are the preferred way to move many rows. UpsertResponse.RecordCreated tells you create vs update.
  • Elastic tables (Cosmos DB-backed): partitioned by partitionid (20 GB per logical partition), no multi-record transactions — a synchronous plug-in failure does not roll back the write like it does on standard tables.

API limit retry policies

Service protection limitThresholdSDK error codeHex
Number of requests6,000 per 5-minute (300 s) sliding window-21470159020x80072322
Execution time20 minutes (1,200 s) combined per 5-minute window-21470159030x80072321
Concurrent requests52 (or higher)-21470158980x80072326
  • Limits are per user (and per web server). Web API returns HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header (seconds). The SDK throws OrganizationServiceFault with a Retry-After TimeSpan in ErrorDetails.
  • Built-in retry: ServiceClient/CrmServiceClient automatically pause and resend after the Retry-After period. Web API clients must implement it (e.g., Polly waiting for Retry-After, exponential back-off if absent). Don't drive logic from the debug headers x-ms-ratelimit-*.
  • Requests/execution-time limits can be exceeded for a window before enforcement; concurrency errors are immediate. Repeated abuse extends the Retry-After.
  • Plug-ins and custom workflow activities are exempt from these limits (they aren't public API calls), but their execution time counts toward the triggering request.
  • Entitlement (request capacity) limits are different: 24-hour, license-based, admin-managed, soft-enforced. Batching doesn't bypass them — every operation inside a batch still counts.
  • Throughput: many small parallel requests beat a few huge batches; start with batch sizes around 10 and tune; let Retry-After set the ceiling; the x-ms-dop-hint response header suggests parallelism.
// Web API retry sketch (C#)
if (response.StatusCode == (HttpStatusCode)429) {
    var wait = response.Headers.RetryAfter?.Delta ?? TimeSpan.FromSeconds(Math.Pow(2, attempt));
    await Task.Delay(wait);                 // honor Retry-After, fall back to exponential back-off
}

Performance, concurrency, transactions and bulk operations

  • Optimistic concurrency: tables with IsOptimisticConcurrencyEnabled (default true for custom tables) compare RowVersion. SDK: UpdateRequest.ConcurrencyBehavior = ConcurrencyBehavior.IfRowVersionMatches. Web API: If-Match with the ETag.
  • Transactions: synchronous plug-in steps share the platform database transaction (throwing rolls back the whole operation); for multi-row atomicity from a client use ExecuteTransaction or a $batch changeset.
  • Bulk: prefer CreateMultiple/UpdateMultiple/UpsertMultiple over loops or ExecuteMultiple; retrieve only needed columns; page with nextLink; parallelize modestly and let throttling feedback guide you.

OAuth and Microsoft Entra authentication

  • Identity provider: Microsoft Entra ID; library: MSAL (ADAL is retired). Register an app: Web app/API (confidential: secret or certificate) or Native (public client). Delegated permission: Dynamics CRM → user_impersonation.
  • Scopes: interactive/public client → https://{org}.crm.dynamics.com/user_impersonation; confidential/server-to-server (client credentials) → https://{org}.crm.dynamics.com/.default.
  • Flows: authorization code (interactive user, delegated); client credentials (app-only; requires a Dataverse application user with a security role; no consent prompt); managed identity (no secret). Prefer a certificate over a client secret in production.
SymptomUsual cause
401Missing, expired or wrong-audience token
403 with a valid tokenNo application user / security role in that environment — an app registration alone does not grant Dataverse access
AADSTS700016Application not found in the tenant (wrong tenant/authority or client ID)
AADSTS7000215Invalid client secret — often the secret ID pasted instead of the secret value

Background operations Preview

Background operations run a custom API asynchronously so the client doesn't wait.

  • SDK: the ExecuteBackgroundOperation message (use a base OrganizationRequest) with Request (the custom API request to run) and optional CallbackUri; the response has BackgroundOperationId and a Location (status monitor).
  • Web API: call the custom API with header Prefer: respond-async → 202 Accepted with Location and x-ms-dyn-backgroundoperationid.
