sections.title: 3.3 Process workloads by using Microsoft Azure Functions
sections.html:
Skills measured: process long-running operations • implement scheduled and event-driven triggers • authenticate to Microsoft Power Platform by using managed identities.

Why Azure Functions

Plug-ins have a 2-minute limit, run in a sandbox and block the transaction; flows have action and duration limits. Move long-running, heavy, scheduled or externally-triggered work to Azure Functions and call back into Dataverse.

RequirementChoose
Run a job on a schedule (nightly sync, cleanup)Timer trigger (CRON/NCRONTAB)
React to a Dataverse event delivered by a webhookHTTP trigger (secured with a function key or, better, Entra auth)
Decoupled, bursty event ingestion from a Dataverse Service Bus endpointService Bus (queue/topic) trigger
Multi-step, stateful, long-running workflow (fan-out/fan-in, human wait, checkpoints)Durable Functions (orchestrator + activities)

Hosting and runtime facts

  • Flex Consumption is the recommended serverless plan (GA, Linux-only, scale to zero, VNet integration). The classic Consumption plan is legacy (Linux Consumption retires in 2028). Premium = pre-warmed instances, no cold start, VNet; Dedicated (App Service) = effectively unbounded run time for long jobs when Durable Functions isn't used.
  • functionTimeout (host.json) sample default is 5 minutes on Consumption (10-minute maximum) — older PL-400 trivia that is still true for that setting, but don't choose the legacy plan for new designs.
  • .NET isolated worker model is the current model (separate process, full DI control); the in-process model is legacy.
  • Function auth levels: anonymous, function (function/host key), admin (master key — never distribute). Prefer Entra ID (App Service authentication) for production. Key Vault references (@Microsoft.KeyVault(...)) resolve app settings through the app's managed identity (needs Key Vault Secrets User).

Authenticate to Power Platform by using managed identities

Two different "managed identity" scenarios — do not confuse them
A. Azure Function → Dataverse (this skill)B. Dataverse plug-in → Azure resource (see §3.1)
DirectionInto Power PlatformOut of Power Platform
SetupEnable system- or user-assigned identity on the Function App → create a Dataverse application user using the identity's Application (client) ID → assign a security roleFederated identity credential (FIC) on a user-assigned managed identity/app registration; pac managed-identity (Preview commands); plug-in package signing
CodeManagedIdentityCredential/DefaultAzureCredential → token for https://{org}.crm.dynamics.com/.defaultIManagedIdentityService in the plug-in
Secrets?None — the standard client-credentials pattern with an identity instead of a secretNone

Alternative non-managed S2S: pac admin create-service-principal registers the Entra app and the Power Platform admin-application record in one step (secret or certificate).

Sources: learn.microsoft.com/azure/azure-functions/ (functions-scale, flex-consumption-plan, functions-host-json, functions-bindings-timer / service-bus-trigger, function-keys-how-to, durable-functions-overview, dotnet-isolated-process-guide); /power-platform/admin/manage-application-users; /power-platform/admin/set-up-managed-identity.

sections.title: 3.4 Configure Power Automate cloud flows and Copilot Studio workflows
sections.html:
Skills measured: implement complex expressions • implement flow control actions including error handling • configure trigger filter and retry policies • develop reusable logic by using child flows • implement authentication for the Dataverse connector by using service principals. (New: Copilot Studio workflows join the group; Key Vault, sensitive-parameter and connector-trigger bullets were dropped.)

Cloud flows, agent flows and workflows — know which is which

Power Automate cloud flowCopilot Studio agent flowCopilot Studio workflow
Built forGeneral automation across apps and servicesDeterministic business processes an agent calls (standard harness)New visual canvas for the reasoning-oriented GitHub Copilot harness: node-level testing, agent handoffs
Deterministic?YesYes — the same input always produces the same output (AI helps build it, not run it)Orchestrates reasoning steps and deterministic steps
LicensingPer user / per flow (Power Automate)Billed by Copilot Studio consumption; no per-flow licenseCopilot Studio consumption
SharingShare, co-own, run-only usersCan't be copied, shared, co-owned or given run-only permissionsLives inside the agent
Called by an agentConvert to an agent flowTrigger "When an agent calls the flow" + action "Respond to the agent"; must be a solution flow—
  • A cloud flow can be converted to an agent flow (edit → change the plan to Copilot Studio → save); the conversion is one-way and the flow must already be in a solution. The Copilot Studio Flows page lists only flows created there.
  • Agent flows can use premium connectors; they can't call desktop flows. Keep heavy data transformation out of flows — push it to Dataverse logic, a custom connector over an Azure Function, or a dataflow.

Complex expressions

NeedExpression
First non-null value / defaultcoalesce(triggerOutputs()?['body/telephone1'], 'n/a')
Current item in a loop; whole loop itemitem() (inside Apply to each) • items('Apply_to_each')
Output/body of an earlier action or triggeroutputs('Get_row')?['body/name'] • body('Get_row') • triggerBody() • triggerOutputs()
Variablesvariables('total')
DatesformatDateTime(utcNow(), 'yyyy-MM-dd') • addDays(utcNow(), -30) (also addHours/addMinutes/addSeconds)
JSON and URLsjson(outputs('Compose')) • uriComponent('a b')
XMLxpath(xml(body('Get_xml')), '//order/@id')
Combine collections / idsunion(arr1, arr2) • guid()
Run metadata / action resultsworkflow() (id, name, tags such as flowDisplayName, environmentName) • result('Scope_name') • actions('Name')

The ?[] operator returns null instead of failing when a property is missing. Expressions are limited to 8,192 characters.

Flow control and error handling

  • Try / Catch / Finally with Scopes: put the normal actions in a Try scope. Add a Catch scope whose Configure run after is has failed / is skipped / has timed out for Try. Add a Finally scope that runs after all four statuses of Try and Catch. Use result('Try') in Catch to inspect failures.
  • Terminate ends the run with a chosen status (Succeeded, Failed, Cancelled) and an error code/message — typically gated by run-after.
  • Other controls: Condition, Switch (25 cases), Apply to each (concurrency default 1, range 1–50), Do until, Parallel branches. Apply to each handles 5,000 items on low-license profiles and 100,000 otherwise.
  • Key limits: 500 actions per flow, 8 nesting levels, run duration 30 days, recurrence 60 s–500 days; flows are auto-turned off after repeated errors (14 days), no trigger activity (90 days) or throttling (14 days).

Trigger filters and retry policies

TechniqueWhere it runsEffect
Trigger conditions (Settings → Trigger conditions; start with @, e.g. @equals(triggerOutputs()?['body/statuscode'], 1))Before the run is createdCheapest: no run is started or logged. Multiple conditions are AND-ed; use @or(...) for OR.
Filter rows ($filter OData) and Select columns ($select) on the Dataverse trigger/actionAt the connector (server-side)Reduces rows/columns pulled and runs triggered
Filter array actionInside the run, client-sideMost expensive: data already retrieved, run already consumed
Retry typeBehavior
defaultExponential back-off, 4 retries for most operations (the policy covers 408, 429 and 5xx responses and connectivity failures)
noneOne attempt only
fixedConstant ISO-8601 interval; count 1–90
exponentialRandom interval within a growing range; count 1–90; optional minimumInterval/maximumInterval

Set it in Settings → Networking → Retry policy on an action or trigger. Dataverse List rows returns up to 5,000 rows by default; turn on Pagination with a Threshold (up to 100,000, in multiples of 5,000) to get more.

Reusable logic with child flows

  • Parent and child must be in a solution. Child trigger: Manually trigger a flow (with inputs); child returns data with Respond to a PowerApp or flow (or the premium Response action). Parent calls it with the built-in Run a Child Flow.
  • On the child's Run only users settings, switch every connection to "Use this connection"; passing the parent's connections through isn't supported (typical error: only embedded connections are supported).
  • The parent waits for the child up to 30 days (1 year when only built-in connectors and Dataverse are used). Put parent and child in the same flow group if they share Process-license capacity.

Authenticate the Dataverse connector with a service principal

  1. Create an Entra app registration / service principal and a client secret (or certificate).
  2. Create a Dataverse application user for it and assign a least-privilege security role that covers the tables/operations.
  3. In the flow designer: Dataverse action → Add new connection → Connect with service principal → client (app) ID, secret, tenant ID.
  • To make the flow itself owned by a service principal: share the connections with it (not needed for solution flows) and set the flow owner (Details → Edit → Owner). A service principal can't be a co-owner.
  • A human who saves a flow using Run only users connections or the trigger's Run as option needs prvActOnBehalfOfAnotherUser (the Delegate role).
  • Why: flows keep running when the person who built them leaves, and permissions are controlled by the application user's role instead of a person's.
Exam traps
  • "Agent flows are deterministic" — true. Agent flows can't be shared/co-owned; cloud flows can.
  • Cheapest way to cut unnecessary runs → trigger condition (beats Filter rows, which beats Filter array).
  • More than 4 retries → switch from default to fixed/exponential (count up to 90).
  • Child flow connection errors → set the child's Run-only users to "Use this connection".
  • More than 5,000 Dataverse rows → Pagination + Threshold.

Sources: learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio/ (flows-overview, flows-faqs, harnesses-overview); /power-automate/ (customize-triggers, create-child-flows, dataverse/list-rows, dataverse/manage-dataverse-connections, service-principal-support, limits-and-config); /azure/logic-apps/ (expression-functions-reference, error-exception-handling).

sections.title: 3.5 Build Microsoft Foundry agents by using code that integrates with Microsoft Power Platform
sections.html:
Skills measured: integrate custom agents by using Power Platform MCP servers • connect custom agents to Copilot Studio agents • integrate custom agents with Dataverse data by using Work IQ • consume Copilot Studio agents by using the Copilot Studio client library. Status tags below come from current docs — several surfaces are Preview, and the exam says it mostly tests GA features.

Foundry in one page

Agent typeWhat it isStatus
Prompt agentInstructions + model + tools; no code to host; author in the portal or via SDK/RESTGA
Hosted agentYour own code/container (Agent Framework, LangGraph, OpenAI Agents SDK, Anthropic SDK, GitHub Copilot SDK) with a managed endpoint, autoscale and its own Entra identityGA
Voice-based prompt agentReal-time speech through Voice LivePreview
  • SDKs: Python azure-ai-projects (AIProjectClient; the older azure-ai-agents is superseded); .NET Azure.AI.Projects (--prerelease); JavaScript @azure/ai-projects.
  • Toolboxes bundle tools (MCP servers, A2A, OpenAPI, Azure AI Search, web search, code interpreter) behind one managed MCP endpoint. The classic connected agents tool is deprecated; use the A2A tool (a2a, protocol v1.0, GA; a2a_preview is the older Preview).
  • Choose Foundry for custom/fine-tuned models, your own agent framework or code, Azure-native hosting/networking, or to call the agent from other code; choose Copilot Studio for business-user authoring, Teams/M365/web channels, and Power Platform governance (data policies, Managed Environments, solutions/pipelines). They interoperate; many solutions use both.

(a) Integrate custom agents by using Power Platform MCP servers

  • Dataverse MCP server endpoint: https://<org>.crm.dynamics.com/api/mcp. Current tools: search_data, search (metadata/skills), create_record, update_record, delete_record (needs explicit user approval), create_table, update_table, delete_table (approval), read_query (SQL SELECT only), describe, upsert_skill/delete_skill, and file-upload/download tools. The old names describe_table, list_tables, fetch were removed and the old data search became search_data — update stale allow-lists.
  • Security: ordinary Dataverse security roles and row-level security apply; there is no separate MCP ACL. Admin control: Power Platform admin center → environment → Settings → Product → Features → Dataverse Model Context Protocol. The Copilot Studio client is enabled by default; other clients (VS Code GitHub Copilot, Copilot CLI, Claude) must be enabled per client (Is Enabled = Yes); governing with Advanced connector policies needs a Managed Environment. Since Dec 15, 2025 calls from agents outside Copilot Studio are billed as Copilot Credits (exempt with Dynamics 365 Premium or a Microsoft 365 Copilot license).
  • From a Foundry agent: add an MCP tool with server_url (the endpoint above) and server_label; authenticate through a project connection (none, custom-keys, oauth2, user-entra-token, project-managed-identity, agentic-identity). Users need the Foundry User role (creating the connection needs Foundry Project Manager). A consent failure surfaces as JSON-RPC error -32006 CONSENT_REQUIRED.
  • Custom MCP servers for Copilot Studio: use the MCP onboarding wizard or a custom connector whose OpenAPI declares x-ms-agentic-protocol: mcp-streamable-1.0. Copilot Studio supports Streamable HTTP only (SSE is deprecated).

(b) Connect custom agents to Copilot Studio agents

DirectionMechanismStatus
Custom code → Copilot Studio agentCopilot Studio client library (direct-to-engine channel) — the production pathGA
Copilot Studio agent → Foundry agentAgents page → Add an agent → Microsoft Foundry (standard harness). The Foundry agent must have the Activity protocol endpoint enabled — only through the REST API or Python SDK, not the portal — and live in the new Foundry portal; otherwise HTTP 400 "endpoint does not support activity"Preview
Copilot Studio agent exposed to external agentsMCP client / A2A client publish channels (Entra app registration, OAuth authorization code; every call carries the user's identity)Preview, GitHub-harness agents, early-release environments

(c) Integrate custom agents with Dataverse data by using Work IQ

  • Work IQ gives agents grounded, permission-aware access to Microsoft 365 work data; Business Applications in Work IQ brings Dataverse / Dynamics 365 / Power Apps context into that layer.
  • Status depends on the surface: the Work IQ MCP endpoint is GA; the Work IQ tool inside Foundry (work_iq_preview), Work IQ inside Copilot Studio (GitHub-harness only) and Business Applications in Work IQ are Preview.
  • Flow from Foundry: the agent calls the Work IQ tool → Foundry forwards over A2A with on-behalf-of (OBO) of the signed-in user → Work IQ honors Microsoft 365 permissions and sensitivity labels. One-time tenant setup needs a Global Administrator to consent to the delegated permission WorkIQAgent.Ask.
  • Microsoft Agent 365 is the governance/registry layer for MCP servers (Work IQ, Microsoft-hosted workload servers, your own).

(d) Consume Copilot Studio agents by using the Copilot Studio client library

LanguagePackageClientKey calls

// CopilotClient is created from the settings plus an authenticated HttpClient (token for CopilotStudio.Copilots.Invoke)

The sample README says service-to-service (app-only) isn't currently supported, while a package description claims it — confirm before relying on it.

AI-assisted development tools

sections.title: 4.1 Publish and consume Dataverse events
sections.html:
Skills measured: publish an event by using IServiceEndpointNotificationService • publish an event by using the Plug-in Registration Tool • register service endpoints (webhooks, Azure Service Bus, Azure Event Hub) • recommend options for listening to Dataverse events.

Publishing an event

  • By configuration: in the Plug-in Registration Tool register a service endpoint (Register New Service Endpoint → Queue, One-way, Two-way, REST, Topic or Event Hub) or a webhook (Register New WebHook, stored in the same ServiceEndpoint table with Contract = 8), then register a step on a message/table (stage, mode, filtering attributes) exactly like a plug-in step.
  • By code: a plug-in (or custom workflow activity) posts its own execution context with IServiceEndpointNotificationService.Execute(EntityReference serviceEndpoint, IExecutionContext context); the body sent is a serialized RemoteExecutionContext. The method returns the endpoint's response string (meaningful for two-way/REST contracts).
var notify = (IServiceEndpointNotificationService)serviceProvider.GetService(typeof(IServiceEndpointNotificationService));
var endpoint = new EntityReference("serviceendpoint", serviceEndpointId);   // the registered endpoint record
string reply = notify.Execute(endpoint, context);                           // posts the execution context

Service endpoint contracts

ContractListener must be online?Returns data to Dataverse?Notes
QueueNo — messages persistNoBuffering; consumer reads when ready
TopicOne or more subscriptionsNoPub/sub for several heterogeneous subscribers
One-wayYesNoNo listener → exponential retry until the job fails
Two-wayYesYes (string)Request/response
RESTYesYesREST analogue of two-way
Event HubN/A (ingestion)NoHigh-volume streaming/telemetry; SAS auth only; body XML or JSON
WebhookYes (HTTP endpoint)Sync steps can surface errorsAlways JSON; ports 80/443 only
  • Message format: .NET binary by default; switch to XML or JSON for non-.NET listeners (Service Bus / Event Hub). Webhooks are always JSON.
  • Size limits: Service Bus / Event Hub — if the HTTP payload exceeds 192 KB, Dataverse strips ParentContext, InputParameters and the images (and flags MessageMaxSizeExceeded); still too big → the send fails. Webhook — the header x-ms-dynamics-msg-size-exceeded appears above 256 KB. Don't swap the two numbers.
  • Webhook authentication: WebhookKey (a code query-string key — built for Azure Functions), HttpHeader (key/value headers) or HttpQueryString. Dataverse always sends x-ms-dynamics-organization, x-ms-dynamics-entity-name, x-ms-dynamics-request-name, x-ms-correlation-request-id.
  • Service Bus authentication: SAS (shared access signature) — the native Dataverse → Service Bus integration documents no Entra ID/managed-identity option (don't confuse it with custom-connector OAuth).
  • Event Grid appears as a contract value on the ServiceEndpoint table (used with business events), but the exam objective names webhooks, Service Bus and Event Hub.

Synchronous or asynchronous?

  • Service Bus posting is asynchronous only; webhooks support both synchronous and asynchronous steps. Asynchronous steps register only on PostOperation and are tracked as system jobs (AsyncOperation). A failed synchronous webhook shows an "Endpoint unavailable" dialog with a downloadable log.
  • Retry: throwing InvalidPluginExecutionException(OperationStatus.Retry, ...) makes the async service retry (4 attempts total). Undelivered one-way posts back off exponentially until the job is aborted (Failed).

Recommending a listening option

RequirementRecommend
Low-code, no infrastructure; react to Dataverse changesPower Automate Dataverse triggers (When a row is added, modified or deleted; When an action is performed for business events)
Simple HTTP callback, language-agnostic, need sync or asyncWebhook (e.g., to an HTTP-triggered Azure Function)
Must buffer, listener may be offline, decoupled consumersService Bus queue
Several independent subscribers get the same eventService Bus topic
Very high volume / telemetry / stream analyticsEvent Hub
Need a return value from the listenerTwo-way or REST contract
Fine-grained, discoverable, cross-system eventsBusiness events (§3.1) delivered to any of the above

sections.title: 4.2 Implement synchronization for Dataverse data
sections.html:
Skills measured: synchronize by using change tracking • develop code that uses alternate keys • synchronize by using the UpsertRequest message.

Change tracking

  • Enable per table (Track changes or EntityMetadata.ChangeTrackingEnabled = true); it cannot be disabled once enabled; not every table is eligible (CanChangeTrackingBeEnabled).
  • SDK: RetrieveEntityChangesRequest (EntityName, Columns, PageInfo, DataVersion). No token = a full snapshot (no deletes). The response (EntityChanges) lists NewOrUpdatedItem and RemovedOrDeletedItem plus DataToken (store it for the next call), MoreRecords and PagingCookie.
  • Web API: send Prefer: odata.track-changes → the response includes @odata.deltaLink; calling it returns only later changes; deletions appear as $deletedEntity items.
  • Limits: one table per request; tokens expire after 7 days by default (Organization.ExpireChangeTrackingInDays) — after that you must re-sync fully; page size defaults to 5,000; caller needs organization-level Read; $filter, $orderby, $expand, $top are not supported with track-changes.

Alternate keys

  • A unique, business-meaningful identifier (e.g., an ERP account number) used instead of the GUID. Create with EntityKeyMetadata + CreateEntityKeyRequest (or the maker portal).
  • Allowed key column types: Decimal Number, Whole Number, Single Line of Text, Date Time, Lookup, Option Set; the columns must not have field-level security. Limits: 10 keys per table, up to 16 columns / 900 bytes per key; not supported on virtual tables. Characters / < > * % & : \ ? + in values break Web API calls.
  • The unique index is built asynchronously: EntityKeyIndexStatus = Pending, In Progress, Active or Failed; retry a failed build with ReactivateEntityKeyRequest. Until it's Active the key can't be used.
  • Use: Web API /accounts(accountnumber='ABC123') (composite: /contacts(firstname='Joe',emailaddress1='a@x.com')); SDK new Entity("account", "accountnumber", "ABC123") or KeyAttributes.

Upsert

var account = new Entity("account", "accountnumber", "ABC123");   // alternate key
account["name"] = "Contoso Ltd";
var result = (UpsertResponse)service.Execute(new UpsertRequest { Target = account });
Console.WriteLine(result.RecordCreated ? "created" : "updated");  // RecordCreated tells you which happened
  • UpsertRequest creates if no match, updates otherwise — slower than a plain create, so use it when existence is unknown (typical for inbound sync). Web API equivalent: PATCH on the alternate-key URL.
  • UpsertMultiple (UpsertMultipleRequest.Targets → Results): the table must support both CreateMultiple and UpdateMultiple; duplicate keys in one payload cause an error (contrast UpdateMultiple, which silently keeps only the first). The Web API action returns 204 with no per-row created/updated flag.
  • On elastic tables, upsert applies directly and does not fire Create/Update events.

Typical sync design: external → Dataverse = alternate key + UpsertMultiple; Dataverse → external = change tracking (delta token) or business events / Service Bus for near-real-time.

sections.title: 4.3 Create custom connectors
sections.html:
Skills measured: authentication • policy templates • import definitions (OpenAPI, Azure services, GitHub) • connector for an Azure service • Azure Function for a connector • extend the OpenAPI definition • code that transforms data.

Creating a connector

PathNotes
From blankManual definition (Power Apps/Power Automate only)
Import an OpenAPI fileOpenAPI 2.0 (Swagger) only — OpenAPI 3.0 isn't supported (convert first); file < 1 MB. Works for Power Apps, Power Automate, Logic Apps and Copilot Studio.
Import a Postman collectionCollection < 1 MB
Import from GitHubWizard pulls from Microsoft's PowerPlatformConnectors repository
From an Azure serviceEntra app registration + OpenAPI for the Azure API (e.g., Resource Manager); for your own Azure Function, front it with API Management and import the APIM-generated OpenAPI
  • CLI: pac connector create | update | download | init | list. Files: apiDefinition.swagger.json, apiProperties.json, an icon, optional script.csx, optional settings file. pac connector init --connection-template NoAuth|BasicAuth|ApiKey|OAuthGeneric|OAuthAAD scaffolds the properties. pac connector list shows only solution-aware connectors. (paconn is the older Python CLI.) Put connectors in a solution for ALM.

Authentication

  • Types: No auth, Basic, API key (header or query), OAuth 2.0 (generic or provider-specific: Microsoft Entra ID, GitHub, Dropbox, Salesforce…). On-premises/Windows auth goes through the on-premises data gateway.
  • OAuth 2.0 uses the authorization code flow. Register the connector's redirect URL in the identity provider's app registration: https://global.consent.azure-apim.net/redirect/<connector-id>.
  • Managed identity can replace the client secret for Entra OAuth (needs a single-tenant app registration — a real tenant ID, not common). Multiple auth types on one connector can't be built in the wizard — hand-edit connectionParameterSets in apiProperties.json.
  • Azure Function backend: protect with a function key (connector API key auth: x-functions-key header or code query parameter) or, better, Entra ID OAuth.

Policy templates (change behavior at runtime without code)

TemplateUse
Set host URLPoint operations at a different host (e.g., per-tenant/region)
Route requestSend an operation to a different endpoint/method/path
Set HTTP headerAdd/override/delete request or response headers
Set query string parameterAdd a fixed or conditional parameter
Set propertySet a value in the request/response body
Convert array to object / Convert object to arrayReshape payloads for the connector schema
Convert delimited string into an array of objectsTurn "a,b,c" style strings into structured arrays

In the OpenAPI they appear as x-ms-apimTemplate-policySection (Request / Response / Failure) and x-ms-apimTemplate-operationName (which operations). "Set connection" and "Transform body" are not real templates.

Extending the OpenAPI definition

ExtensionPurpose
x-ms-summary, summary, descriptionFriendly labels and help text in the designer
x-ms-visibilityimportant (shown first) / advanced (collapsed) / internal (hidden; required internal params need a default)
x-ms-dynamic-values / x-ms-dynamic-listPopulate a drop-down from another operation

Agents and MCP: a custom connector can expose an MCP server to Copilot Studio when the OpenAPI declares x-ms-agentic-protocol: mcp-streamable-1.0 on the MCP POST operation (§1.2). This extension isn't on the canonical extensions page, so treat it as a Copilot Studio-specific convention.

Custom code (script.csx) — transform data

public class Script : ScriptBase                       // class must be named Script and derive from ScriptBase
{
    public override async Task<HttpResponseMessage> ExecuteAsync()
    {
        var response = await this.Context.SendAsync(this.Context.Request, this.CancellationToken).ConfigureAwait(false);
        if (this.Context.OperationId == "GetOrderSummary" && response.IsSuccessStatusCode)
        {
            var body = JObject.Parse(await response.Content.ReadAsStringAsync().ConfigureAwait(false));
            var summary = new JObject { ["orderId"] = body["id"], ["lineCount"] = ((JArray)body["lines"]).Count };
            response.Content = CreateJsonContent(summary.ToString());
        }
        return response;
    }
}
  • Custom code takes precedence over the codeless definition and is for payload transformations that policy templates can't do. One script file per connector; file ≤ 1 MB; must finish within 2 minutes (a raised limit — new connectors get it automatically; update an existing connector to pick it up); targets .NET Standard 2.0 with an allow-list of namespaces (System.*, Newtonsoft.Json, Microsoft.Extensions.Logging, …).
  • Use this.Context.SendAsync for outbound calls (don't build your own HttpClient); this.Context exposes OperationId, Request, CorrelationId, Logger. OperationId can arrive base64-encoded in some regions. Not available with the on-premises data gateway. In a VNet-linked environment SendAsync reaches only public endpoints.

Governance, sharing and certification

  • Data policies (DLP): classify as Business, Non-Business (default) or Blocked. Environment admins classify custom connectors by name; tenant admins by Host URL pattern (the * catch-all rule goes last). A resource can't mix Business and Non-Business connectors.
  • Share inside the tenant directly (Can view / Can edit) or through app/flow sharing; certification by Microsoft is needed to publish for other tenants. Independent publishers add "(Independent Publisher)"; a custom icon needs a verified publisher.
Exam traps for Domain 4
  • Only Two-way and REST contracts return data. Service Bus is async-only; webhooks do both. 192 KB (Service Bus/Event Hub) vs 256 KB (webhook).
  • OpenAPI 3.0 can't be imported — convert to 2.0. pac connector list lists only solution-aware connectors.
  • Policy template names are exactly the eight above. Custom code: 2 minutes / 1 MB / one file.
  • Change-tracking token expiry (7 days) → full re-sync. Change tracking can't be turned off. UpdateMultiple ignores duplicate keys; UpsertMultiple errors.
  • Alternate key index still building (Pending/In Progress) → calls by key fail until it is Active.

Sources: learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/ — azure-integration, register-web-hook, use-webhooks, register-plug-in, use-change-tracking-synchronize-data-external-systems, define-alternate-keys-entity, use-alternate-key-reference-record, bulk-operations; /connectors/custom-connectors/ — define-openapi-definition, write-code, policy-templates, openapi-extensions, certification-submission.

sections.title: Overview
sections.html:
The exam measures applied knowledge: you are expected to have built things. Every week below pairs reading with a lab, and ends with a checkpoint against the Skills checklist. The plan front-loads the heaviest domain (Domain 3, 35–40%) and gives the new material (code apps, Foundry agents, MCP, Work IQ) its own weeks, because Microsoft has not yet published Learn paths for it — you will learn it from product documentation and samples.

Lab environment checklist
  • A Power Platform developer/trial environment with Dataverse (and a second environment for ALM and Pipelines labs)
  • An Azure subscription (free account works): Functions, Service Bus, Application Insights, Key Vault, Foundry project
  • VS Code (+ Power Platform Tools extension), .NET SDK, Node.js LTS, Git, Python 3
  • Power Platform CLI (pac) and the Power Apps CLI (pa) — they are different tools
  • Plug-in Registration Tool (pac tool prt), a REST client (Postman or VS Code REST Client)
  • Microsoft Entra permissions to create app registrations and federated credentials

Some labs need premium capabilities (Managed Environments for Pipelines, Power Apps Premium to run code apps). Use a trial or developer environment for those.

sections.title: Study habits that work for this exam
sections.html:
• Build, then read. Do the lab first, then read the doc to see what you missed.
  • Memorize the exact names: stage numbers, message names, CLI verbs and switches, header names, manifest elements.
  • Practice the decision, not just the definition. For every feature, write "choose it when / don't choose it when".
  • Keep a trap log. Every missed question becomes one line: what I picked, why it was wrong.
  • Mix old and new. The exam blends carried-over and new topics in the same scenario (for example, a plug-in that uses a managed identity to call an Azure service).
  • Read docs dated 2026. Several features changed name or syntax (e.g., pa vs pac code).

parts.title: Exam-day plan
parts.subtitle: Preparation, pacing, tools allowed, break rules and the last-minute facts worth re-reading

sections.title: Exam-day plan
sections.html:
The week before

  • Take the full timed practice exam twice, a few days apart; fix every row below 4 in the skills checklist.
  • Skim the cheat sheets (numbers, commands, GA/Preview) and your trap log — don't start new topics.
  • Run the exam sandbox (aka.ms/examdemo) once so the interface (flagging, review screen, case-study layout, Learn button) is familiar.
  • Online exam? Test your system with Pearson VUE's check, clear your desk and room, have government ID ready. Test center? Confirm the address and arrival time.
  • Re-check the study guide's change log in case Microsoft revised the skills list.

During the exam

TopicApproach
PacingWith 40–60 questions in about 100 minutes you have roughly 1.5–2.5 minutes per question. Aim to be a third of the way through at the one-third mark. Don't spend more than ~3 minutes on any single item on the first pass.
First passAnswer what you know, flag what you don't. Answer every question before time runs out — an unanswered item can't earn credit.
EliminationCross out answers that use deprecated or wrong-direction features (e.g., Xrm.Page, pac code, SSE for MCP, OpenAPI 3.0 import, a function key where an Entra identity is required). Many questions have two plausible options — look for the constraint (GA vs Preview, sync vs async, same transaction vs not, least privilege).
Multi-selectCount how many answers are requested ("Select TWO"); each must be independently correct.
Code and CLI itemsRead the code once for what it does, then compare with the requirement. Check stage number, mode, message name, header, scope and package name before the logic.
Case studiesSkim the questions first, then read the scenario for the requirements/constraints that matter (identity, volume, latency, licensing, governance). Re-read the exhibit instead of relying on memory. Breaks are allowed in case studies, but you can't return to questions seen before the break.
Microsoft Learn buttonAvailable in a split screen (no extra time; Q&A, practice assessments and your profile are blocked). Use it only to confirm a specific detail — a header name, a table column, a limit — with Ctrl+F on the page. If you can't find it in 90 seconds, make your best choice and flag it.
Breaks5 minutes are built into the exam time; the clock keeps running during a break, and after a break you can't go back to earlier questions. You can't break in the middle of a lab or a problem/solution question set. Use the restroom before you start.
ReviewUse the review screen for flagged items. Change an answer only if you can name the specific fact that makes the first choice wrong.

High-yield last-minute facts

Names and numbers

  • Stages: 10 / 20 / (30 internal) / 40; async only on 40; images: no pre on Create, no post on Delete
  • Plug-in limit 2 minutes; depth 8; .NET Framework 4.6.2–4.8
  • Service protection: 6,000 / 5 min, 20 min execution, 52 concurrent; 429 + Retry-After
  • Web API: no $skip; page size max 5,000; $batch ≤ 1,000
  • Change-tracking token 7 days; alternate keys 10 per table
  • Service Bus/Event Hub payload 192 KB; webhook 256 KB
  • Custom connector code 1 MB / 2 min / one file; OpenAPI 2.0 only

Traps to avoid

  • pa app ... is the current code-app CLI; pac code ... is legacy/Preview
  • CreateOrganizationService(null) = SYSTEM
  • Function→Dataverse managed identity (application user) ≠ plug-in managed identity (FIC)
  • Code apps: only solution-aware instant flows with the Power Apps trigger
  • ExecuteCopilotAsyncV2 is the reliable Copilot Studio call from a code app
  • Work IQ / MCP widgets / Copilot Studio→Foundry: check the surface for GA vs Preview
  • Agent flows: deterministic, not shareable; trigger conditions beat Filter array

After the exam

  • You get a pass/fail result and a score report showing your performance by skill area. If you fail, use it to decide where to focus; wait 24 hours before the first retake, then 14 days between later attempts (max 5 in 12 months).
  • Passing earns Microsoft Certified: Power Platform Developer Associate — set a calendar reminder: renewal opens six months before the one-year expiry and is free.
